                    ### Question
                    A 12-year-old male presents to the pediatrician after two days of tea-colored urine which appeared to coincide with the first day of junior high football. He explains that he refused to go back to practice because he was humiliated by the other players due to his quick and excessive fatigue after a set of drills accompanined by pain in his muscles. A blood test revealed elevated creatine kinase and myoglobulin levels. A muscle biopsy was performed revealing large glycogen deposits and an enzyme histochemistry showed a lack of myophosphorylase activity. Which of the following reactions is not occuring in this individuals?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Converting glucose-6-phosphate to glucose
opb. Breaking down glycogen to glucose-1-phosphate
opc. Cleaving alpha-1,6 glycosidic bonds from glycogen
opd. Creating alpha-1,6 glycosidic bonds in glycogen
ope. Converting galactose to galactose-1-phosphate

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient presents with symptoms consistent with McArdle's disease, characterized by a deficiency in myophosphorylase, which is essential for glycogenolysis. The lack of myophosphorylase activity leads to impaired glycogen breakdown, specifically the inability to convert glycogen to glucose-1-phosphate. This aligns with the elevated creatine kinase and myoglobulin levels indicating muscle damage due to inadequate energy supply during exercise. Therefore, the following reactions are affected: 1) Breaking down glycogen to glucose-1-phosphate (option opb) is not occurring due to the enzyme deficiency. 2) Converting glucose-6-phosphate to glucose (option opa) is also impaired as glycogen accumulation leads to increased glucose-6-phosphate levels, but this reaction can still occur in other contexts. 3) Cleaving alpha-1,6 glycosidic bonds from glycogen (option opc) is not occurring due to the lack of myophosphorylase. 4) Creating alpha-1,6 glycosidic bonds in glycogen (option opd) is not directly affected by the deficiency. 5) Converting galactose to galactose-1-phosphate (option ope) is unrelated to glycogen metabolism. Thus, the most definitive answer is that the reaction 'Breaking down glycogen to glucose-1-phosphate' (option opb) is not occurring.
